scholarships.title: LSE PhD Studentships
scholarships.official_source: London School of Economics and Political Science

eligibility: Students of all nationalities, including both UK and international students
Research proposed in any LSE discipline
Complete LSE PhD admission application, including references, submitted by the departmental funding deadline
Outstanding academic merit and research potential
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to high calibre students of all nationalities across all LSE research areas. Selection is based solely on outstanding academic merit and research potential. There is no separate studentship application; eligibility is decided through the LSE PhD admission application, which must be complete, including references, by the relevant departmental funding deadline.
benefits: Full tuition fees for four years
Open to UK and international students of all nationalities
documents: Complete LSE PhD admission application, including research proposal and references, submitted by the departmental funding deadline
application_method: There is no separate application for LSE PhD Studentships
Submit a complete application for admission to an LSE research programme through the LSE Application System
Ensure the application is complete, including references, by the funding deadline set by your academic department
Your academic department nominates you for consideration by a School panel for all funding opportunities you are eligible for
existing.selection_notes: Academic departments nominate students for consideration by a School panel for all PhD funding opportunities they may be eligible for. Awards are made solely on the basis of outstanding academic merit and research potential, assessed on both past academic record and likely aptitude to complete a PhD in the time allocated.
existing.duration: Tenable for four years, renewed annually subject to satisfactory academic performance
existing.application_period: Applications for entry in 2027/28 open in October 2026. Funding decisions for the first round fall at the 3 December 2026 and 13 January 2027 funding panels.
existing.deadline_display: 3 December 2026 - some departments set this early deadline; 13 January 2027 - main first deadline guaranteeing consideration for initial LSE PhD Studentships; 27 May 2027 - final second deadline for department-selected studentships, unawarded LSE PhD Studentships and self-funders only

scholarships.title: LSE Excellence Scholarship
scholarships.official_source: London School of Economics and Political Science

eligibility: Applying to a Postgraduate Taught programme in an eligible LSE department: Accounting, Anthropology, Gender Studies, Geography and Environment, Health Policy, International Development, International History, LSE Law School, Mathematics, Media and Communications, School of Public Policy, Sociology or Statistics
Demonstrating outstanding academic ability and strong potential to thrive in the chosen programme
For double degree programmes, first year of study must be at LSE
Not applying to an executive education programme
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to applicants to Postgraduate Taught programmes in a specified list of LSE departments who demonstrate outstanding academic ability and strong potential to thrive in their chosen programme. Applicants to double degree programmes qualify only if their first year of study is at LSE, and applicants to executive education programmes are not eligible. No separate financial support application is required.
benefits: GBP 10,000 per year if enrolled on a two-year programme
No separate financial support application required
coverage: Cash award of GBP 20,000 in total toward study costs, with no breakdown of what it pays for published by LSE
application_method: Submit an application for admission to an eligible LSE postgraduate taught programme
No financial support application is required; awardees are identified from the admission application
Submit early, as awards are made on a rolling basis until all awards are allocated
existing.selection_notes: Recognises applicants who demonstrate outstanding academic ability and strong potential to thrive in their chosen programme. Awards are made on a rolling basis during the application cycle until all awards are allocated, so earlier strong applications have an advantage.
existing.notes: Funding period: total over the programme; GBP 10,000 per year for two-year programmes
